doc.title: Bernard Purdie interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003

title: Childhood listening and country music; playing simply
summary: He heard gospel, country, blues and western, loves Floyd Cramer and Ray Charles as country, and learned to play simply and groove.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: We didn’t talk much about your childhood. What music were you hearing in your house when you were a little kid?

Gospel, country, blues. And western. And all kinds of things like that. One of my all-time favorites is the Floyd Cramer. I’m country — I just love country music. Always did. And the funniest part, here’s what people used to laugh at me when I used to say Ray Charles is country. And they’d say what are you talking about, Ray Charles — Ray Charles ain’t country. I’d say Ray Charles is country. Every song that Ray Charles has recorded has © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-
been a country song. It’s that simple. He likes melodies. He likes strong lyrics that have meaning, and that’s what you get from country. It’s really that simple.

Well you know I can see why you would — with what you’ve said about just the groove of a song and the meaning of a song — why you would like something like Floyd Cramer. Because it’s not about technique and lots of notes, it’s just about the simplicity and nice feel.

And that’s what I had to do all my life. Learn to be simple. When I play I play simple. I am right down the middle. And I know how to go from one side to the other without a problem. I don’t have a problem. Because I’m going to be the simplest person in there. But yet I’m going to groove with it. That is part of my whole life. All my life I was taught that. I was taught that’s what you need to do, that’s what you need to focus on. You focus in on the music. You focus everything about what you have to do. And that’s the ABCs of the music business. But I really did. I learned about the music business. It wasn’t just being a player. If it was just being a player I’d have been what I would call a superstar. I’d have been a James Brown with the instrumental thing and being the artist. I’d have been there umpteen years ago. But I play every kind of music so I have always wanted to play every kind of music. And I brought you a CD that really shows ten different ways, at least ten different ways of Bernard Purdie.
